I will keep the usual wheat-maize rotation on my land this year. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to hold yield and reduce risk, because the climate, irrigation habits, and local market all fit it well. At the start of the year, my wheat is already in the field from autumn sowing, so I will focus first on topdressing, watering, and disease control to protect grain formation. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize immediately, because grabbing soil moisture and heat is important here and maize follows wheat smoothly on the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed, put most fertilizer on the two grain crops rather than trying something risky, irrigate enough to protect yield but not waste water, and keep tillage simple so I can turn the crop fast between seasons. I am doing this because I know the system, it matches my labor and schooling level, and it gives me the most dependable annual output.
